objectives: To assess the impact of GLP-1 receptor agonists on all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), and major adverse kidney events (MAKE) in adult kidney transplant recipients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, and to synthesize the limited available evidence to inform future research and clinical practice in this population.
inclusion_criteria: Studies were eligible if they included adult (>=18 years) kidney transplant recipients with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed either before or after transplantation, treated with any GLP-1 receptor agonist, reported at least one of the following outcomes: all-cause mortality, MACE, or MAKE, and used either a randomized controlled trial design or an observational design (prospective or retrospective cohort study).
exclusion_criteria: Studies were excluded if they lacked a comparator group; were case reports, case series, editorials, letters, conference abstracts, or reviews; or did not report at least one primary outcome or provide sufficient data to extract effect estimates. Conference abstracts were specifically excluded because only full-text, peer-reviewed studies were considered eligible so that included data were complete, verifiable, and suitable for quality assessment.
pmid_query: ("Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonists"[Mesh] OR "GLP-1 receptor agonist*" OR "GLP-1" OR "GLP-1 analogue" OR "Liraglutide" OR "Semaglutide" OR "Dulaglutide" OR "Exenatide" OR "Lixisenatide") AND ("Kidney transplant recipient" OR "Renal transplant recipient" OR "Kidney transplantation" OR "Renal transplantation" OR "Post-transplant patients" OR "Kidney allograft" OR "Renal allograft" OR "Graft function" OR "Transplant patients"); searched in PubMed and adapted for Embase and Cochrane Library from inception to July 2025, with no language restrictions and manual screening of reference lists.
selection_evidence: Results state that after full-text assessment, 4 studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the final analysis. Table 1 then lists exactly four included studies with numbered references: Cohen et al. 2025 [19], Orandi et al. 2025 [17], Lin et al. 2025 [18], and Sahi et al. 2025 [21]. Results sections cross-check the same set: the mortality leave-one-out analysis explicitly names Lin, Sahi, and Orandi, while the MAKE/Table 2 definitions explicitly name Orandi, Lin, and Cohen. The reference list confirms that refs 17, 18, 19, and 21 are the corresponding literature studies.
